title: BigQuery Analysis and AI Layer: Visual Guide
outline: Title: BigQuery Analysis and AI Layer: Visual Guide

1. Bytes To Answers | a 2 TB dashboard query with projection, partition pruning, a materialized view and BI Engine switched on one at a time | acceleration is built on top of physical design, never instead of it — an unbounded scan stays 2,048 GB however many accelerators you add, and a view that does not cover the query is simply not selected

2. The Staleness Dial | max_staleness dragged from 0 to 8 hours against two workloads, showing freshness gap, rows merged per query and latency | staleness trades freshness for predictable latency and never trades correctness; four hours is right for a dashboard that stated it and wrong for a fraud alert that inherited it

3. Why It Was Slow | five jobs with identical 96-second wall times and different statistics, each with a fix to choose | wall time names no cause — bytes, shuffle output, spill, the slowest-to-median worker ratio and queue time separate scan-bound from shuffle-bound from skewed from concurrency-limited from plan complexity, and SQL cannot fix a capacity queue

4. Model Then Manifest | the six steps from an object table over 1,000 PDFs to a reconciled manifest, with a toggle for reading the per-row status column and one for swapping the embedding model | a completed embedding job is not complete data: unread status hides 310 missing chunks, and changing model or dimensionality creates a new vector space and normally a new index

5. Recall Versus Speed | VECTOR_SEARCH over 8.6M vectors, exact against an index, with the candidate set widened and the permission filter moved either side of the search | approximate search buys speed by not looking everywhere, so recall@10 is a measurement against brute force rather than a property of the index — and filtering after the search returns too few eligible rows and lets candidates cross the trust boundary first
